text.p: Following are some major events to have taken place on June 16 in history:
1722 - John Churchill, first Duke of Marlborough, died; he led British and Allied armies to important victories over the French in the War of the Spanish Succession.
1858 - Gustav V, king of Sweden (1907-50), born; during his reign he kept Sweden neutral during both world wars.
1869 - Charles Sturt, English explorer who led several expeditions into the interior of Australia, died.
1874 - Arthur Meighen, Canadian prime minister (1920-21; 1926), born.
1890 - Stan Laurel, British film comedian and half of film duo Laurel and Hardy, born.
1930 - Elmer Ambrose Sperry, U.S. inventor of the gyroscopic compass, died.
1940 - In France, Marshal Philippe Petain was asked to form a new government following the resignation of Paul Reynaud.
1941 - President Franklin D. Roosevelt ordered the closure by July 10 of all German consulates in the United States.
1952 - A Swedish rescue plane searching for a lost aircraft was shot down by Soviet fighters over Swedish territorial waters.
1955 - Argentine naval officers directed an attack on President Juan Peron's headquarters; the army remained loyal and suppressed the revolt.

1958 - Imre Nagy, Hungarian prime minister during the 1956 uprising crushed by Soviet tanks, was hanged for treason. On this day in 1989 he was reburied after an emotional funeral that brought at least a quarter of a million people on to Budapest's streets.
1961 - Russian ballet dancer Rudolf Nureyev requested asylum in France while in Paris with the Kirov ballet.
1963 - Valentina Tereshkova became the first women to travel into space when she was launched in the Soviet spacecraft Vostok 6.
1969 - Earl Alexander of Tunis, British field marshal during World War Two, died. He directed the British troop evacuation from Dunkirk, France, in 1940.
1975 - The Simonstown agreement on naval cooperation between Britain and South Africa was formally ended by mutual agreement after 169 years.

1976 - Thousands of school children in Soweto, the sprawling black township adjoining Johannesburg, revolted against government plans to enforce Afrikaans as the language for instruction in black schools.
1977 - The Supreme Soviet elected Leonid Brezhnev to the post of president to replace Nikolai Podgorny.
1977 - Wernher von Braun, German-U.S. rocket engineer, died; he designed the German V1 and V2 rockets and later worked for NASA.
1979 - Gen. Ignatius Kutu Acheampong, former military ruler of Ghana (1972-78), was executed for corruption.
1983 - Yuri Andropov was elected chairman of the Presidium of the Supreme Soviet, a position equivalent to president.
1984 - Wilson Ferreira Aldunate, a popular Uruguayan opposition leader, was arrested upon his return from 11 years' exile.

1992 - In Washington, U.S. President George Bush welcomed Russian President Boris Yeltsin as a modern-day Peter the Great to begin a summit where they agreed in principle to slash strategic weapons arsenals by about two-thirds by 2003.
